4. Defendant Nos. 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 contested the suit by filling a joint written statement contending, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable and it is barred under section 46 of the Ain, 2003. Defendant No. 1-Company is doing its business by producing and marketing CI sheet GP sheet etc. The company is doing financial transaction with the Bank since 1987. On 9-10-2001 the company made a representation to the Bank praying for reschedule of the loan taken earlier. In reply thereto, the Bank vide its letter dated 11-10-2001 expressed concern over renewal of the loan upon imposing certain terms and conditions, which were accepted by the defendants but subsequently, the Bank did not take any initiative to that effect, in consequence thereof the defendants suffered huge losses and, as such, the defendants claimed Taka 92,98,90,299 to the Bank as compensation. Thereafter, the Bank took initiative to settle the matter amicably and called a settlement meeting on 24-10-2004. Accordingly, a meeting was held between the high officials of the parties and a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between the Bank and the defendants. Pursuant to the MoU the defendants had fulfilled certain conditions but the Bank violated the terms and conditions of the MoU and illegally demanded Taka 54,22,49,155.85 from the company, which is against the mandate of section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (in short, the Ain, 2003). In the premises, the defendants filed Other Suit No. 186/2007 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong against the Bank praying for a direction upon the Bank to perform its obligations as per the MoU. The Bank appeared in the above suit but thereafter filed the instant suit as of counter of the defendants' suit. The MoU has not yet been cancelled by the Bank in writing and, as such, during subsistence of the MoU, the instant suit is not maintainable.
